author: jwise-mfg
body:
Update related responses and implementation guide to ensure graph is always traversable. This requires all relationships have an inverse. This addresses #230 and properly addresses #220.

**Summary**
Starting from any known node, a client can fully traverse the graph using only POST /objects/related because:

  1. relationships is always returned — every returned object includes its own outgoing edges, so the client immediately knows what nodes are reachable from there without a separate lookup call. This is the key enabler of traversal.
  2. sourceRelationship identifies the traversed edge — tells the client why each object is in the result (e.g. "you got here via SuppliesTo"), which matters when a node has multiple unfiltered relationships returning heterogeneous objects.
  3. Bidirectionality is mandated — if A→B exists, B→A must also be stored. This means querying any node's related objects will surface all its neighbors, so no node is reachable only from one direction. Starting anywhere, you can get everywhere.
  4. reverseOf is required on all relationship types — so a client can always resolve the inverse of any edge it encounters, enabling it to understand the full semantics of the graph without guessing.

Together these mean: pick any node, call /objects/related, follow the relationships fields on what comes back, repeat — and you will eventually reach every connected node with full edge context at each step.

body:
# Pull Request

## Summary

### ✨ New Features
1. **SpeedCondition**: A new condition that evaluates an entity's speed against a threshold with configurable comparison rules, directional decomposition (longitudinal/lateral/magnitude), and coordinate systems (world/entity-frame)
2. **ComparisonRule shared module**: Extracted `ComparisonRule` enum and `compare()` helper into a reusable `comparison.py` module
3. **ElapsedTimeCondition with ComparisonRule**: Added optional `rule` and `tolerance` parameters to express "elapsed time greater than / less than / equal to" semantics (backward-compatible, defaults to `GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUAL`)
4. **Intersection passing scenario speed check**: NPC fails if speed drops below 5 km/h during intersection traversal

---

## 🔍 Root Cause Analysis

### Problem Description
The scenario framework lacked a speed-based condition for triggering scenario events, and `ComparisonRule` was tightly coupled to `SpeedCondition`, preventing reuse by other conditions like `ElapsedTimeCondition`.

### Technical Details
- `SpeedCondition` fills the gap for speed-based pass/fail evaluation
- Extracting `ComparisonRule` to a shared module enables any condition to use comparison operators consistently
- `ElapsedTimeCondition` previously only supported `>=` semantics; now it supports all five comparison operators

---

## 🛠️ Changes

### 1. `conditions/comparison.py` — NEW
- `ComparisonRule` enum: `GREATER_THAN`, `LESS_THAN`, `EQUAL_TO`, `GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUAL`, `LESS_THAN_OR_EQUAL`
- `compare()` helper function used by both `SpeedCondition` and `ElapsedTimeCondition`

### 2. `conditions/speed.py` — NEW
- `SpeedCondition` class extending `BaseCondition`
- `SpeedDirection` enum: `LONGITUDINAL`, `LATERAL`, `MAGNITUDE`
- `SpeedCoordinateSystem` enum: `WORLD`, `ENTITY`
- Entity-frame decomposition using reference entity's forward vector

### 3. `conditions/elapsed_time.py` — MODIFIED
- Added `rule` parameter (default: `ComparisonRule.GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUAL` for backward compatibility)
- Added `tolerance` parameter for `EQUAL_TO` comparisons
- Delegates to shared `compare()` function

### 4. `examples/intersection_passing.py` — MODIFIED
- Added `SpeedCondition` fail condition: scenario fails if NPC speed drops below 5 km/h

### 5. Package exports and `__init__.py` updates
- `ComparisonRule` imported from `comparison.py` (not `speed.py`)
- `SpeedCondition`, `SpeedDirection`, `SpeedCoordinateSystem` added to public API

---

## ✅ Testing

Pre-commit checks:
- [x] ruff (linting)
- [x] ruff-format (formatting)
- [x] mypy (type checking)
- [x] pytest (unit tests)

Manual testing:
- 25+ tests for `SpeedCondition` covering all comparison rules, world/entity coordinate systems, edge cases
- 8 tests for `ElapsedTimeCondition` with `ComparisonRule` (all operators, tolerance, backward compatibility, validation)

---

## 📊 Expected Results

- ✅ Scenarios can trigger events based on entity speed thresholds
- ✅ Directional speed evaluation (longitudinal/lateral) in world and entity frames
- ✅ `ElapsedTimeCondition` supports flexible time comparisons (e.g. "fail if elapsed < 3s")
- ✅ `ComparisonRule` is reusable by any future condition type
- ✅ Intersection passing scenario fails if NPC slows below 5 km/h

---

## ⚠️ Breaking Changes

**None** — `ElapsedTimeCondition` defaults to `GREATER_THAN_OR_EQUAL`, preserving original behavior.

---

author: devin-ai-integration[bot]
body:
## What

Resolves https://github.com/airbytehq/oncall/issues/11603:
- https://github.com/airbytehq/oncall/issues/11603

Related to https://github.com/airbytehq/airbyte/issues/74726:
- https://github.com/airbytehq/airbyte/issues/74726

The `OAuthAuthenticator` in the Bulk CDK `load-http` toolkit had `isTokenExpired()` hardcoded to `return false`. This caused destination connectors with short-lived OAuth tokens (e.g., HubSpot's 30-minute tokens) to fail with HTTP 401 (`EXPIRED_AUTHENTICATION`) once the initial token expired mid-sync.

## How

- Parse the `expires_in` field from the OAuth token response in `refreshAccessToken()`
- Track the computed expiry time in a new `tokenExpiresAt: Instant?` field
- Implement proper expiry checking in `isTokenExpired()` with a 60-second safety buffer before actual expiry
- Inject a `Clock` parameter (defaulting to `Clock.systemUTC()`) for deterministic testing

**Backward compatible**: If the OAuth response does not include `expires_in` (e.g., Salesforce), `tokenExpiresAt` remains `null` and `isTokenExpired()` returns `false` — identical to the previous behavior.

## Review guide

1. `OAuthAuthenticator.kt` — the core fix. Key areas:
   - `isTokenExpired()` (line ~60): replaces hardcoded `return false` with actual expiry check
   - `refreshAccessToken()` (line ~97): now captures `expires_in` from token response
   - **Thread safety**: `accessToken` and `tokenExpiresAt` are non-volatile mutable fields. The original code already had this pattern for `accessToken`; this PR doesn't worsen it but doesn't fix it either. Worth discussing if this needs `@Volatile` or synchronization.
   - **60-second buffer**: `EXPIRY_BUFFER_SECONDS = 60` — is this appropriate for all use cases?

2. `OAuthAuthenticatorTest.kt` — three new test cases covering: token not yet expired, token expired (triggers refresh), and backward compatibility when `expires_in` is absent.

## User Impact

Destination connectors using `OAuthAuthenticator` with APIs that have short-lived tokens (like HubSpot's 30-minute expiry) will now automatically refresh tokens before they expire, preventing HTTP 401 failures during long-running syncs.

No impact on connectors whose OAuth responses don't include `expires_in` (e.g., Salesforce).

## Can this PR be safely reverted and rolled back?

- [x] YES 💚

author: copilot
body:
The on-chip SRAM now matches the `sync_dpram` read timing model with a 2-cycle registered read path and explicit block-RAM inference attributes. The SRAM peripheral and its tests are updated to absorb the added latency, and the ECP5 timing report is refreshed with the measured post-change utilization/Fmax impact.

- **SRAM RTL**
  - Update `rtl/common/memory/sram.sv` to add an internal read pipeline stage.
  - Preserve existing behavior that consumers rely on:
    - byte write masking
    - bounded depth (`DEPTH`)
    - read-first same-address read/write semantics
  - Add block-RAM synthesis attributes on the internal memory array.

- **SRAM peripheral timing**
  - Update `rtl/common/peripherals/sram_peripheral.sv` to insert the extra wait state required for aligned reads.
  - Extend split-read sequencing so cross-word loads still return correctly with the deeper SRAM pipeline.
  - Keep write behavior unchanged apart from the timing needed to pair correctly with the new read path.

- **Test updates**
  - Adjust direct SRAM tests to expect the new 2-cycle read latency while continuing to cover read-first behavior.
  - Adjust SRAM-peripheral latency expectations:
    - aligned reads now complete one cycle later
    - split reads account for the pipelined SRAM read path

- **ECP5 impact documentation**
  - Refresh `rtl/fpga/TIMING_ANALYSIS_ECP5.md` with the new measured ECP5 utilization and routed timing results.
  - Document that the previously reported SRAM readback path is no longer the top routed critical path.

Example of the SRAM timing change:

```systemverilog
(* ram_style = "block" *) logic [31:0] mem [0:DEPTH-1];
logic [31:0] read_data_pipe;

always_ff @(posedge clk) begin
    if (we) begin
        if (wmask[0]) mem[waddr][7:0]   <= wdata[7:0];
        if (wmask[1]) mem[waddr][15:8]  <= wdata[15:8];
        if (wmask[2]) mem[waddr][23:16] <= wdata[23:16];
        if (wmask[3]) mem[waddr][31:24] <= wdata[31:24];
    end

    read_data_pipe <= mem[raddr];
    rdata <= read_data_pipe;
end
```

author: tacascer
body:
## Summary

- Fix `rlocation!` failing to find the SPA in manifest-based runfiles mode (used by `bazel run`). The manifest maps `dist/` as a single entry, but the code was looking up `dist/browser` which doesn't exist as a separate key. Now resolves `dist/` first, then appends `browser/`.
- Replace `eprintln!` with structured `tracing` logs and add info/warn messages for SPA resolution success/failure.

## Root cause

Bazel runfiles have two modes: **directory-based** (symlink tree) and **manifest-based** (flat file mapping). `bazel run` uses manifest mode, where `rlocation!` does exact key lookups. Since `ng_application` exposes `dist/` as a single output artifact, only `dist` appears in the manifest — not subdirectories like `dist/browser`.

Closes #63

## Test plan

- [x] `aspect build //build-scan/server/src:main` succeeds
- [x] `bazel run //build-scan/server/src:main` logs `Serving SPA from Bazel runfiles`
- [x] `curl http://localhost:3000/web/` returns HTTP 200

- Score recovers from 54 -> 80 (the `tar` vulnerability was an error-severity security finding with 2x weight)
- Version is now consistent everywhere: CLI `--version`, JSON output, interactive header, scan header

body:
### Motivation

- Prevent an ABI-encoding mismatch where `GBridgeReceiver` used packed low-level calldata (`abi.encodePacked(...)`) that could be incompatible with the declared `INativeMintPrecompile.mint(address,uint256)` interface and cause bridge mints to fail and events to be dropped.

### Description

- Replace the packed low-level precompile call with an ABI-compatible invocation using `INativeMintPrecompile(SystemAddresses.NATIVE_MINT_PRECOMPILE).mint(recipient, amount)` and preserve failure semantics via `try/catch` that reverts with `MintFailed` on error.
- Update the unit test setup to mock the precompile by selector prefix using `abi.encodeWithSelector(INativeMintPrecompile.mint.selector)` so mock calls match the ABI-style calldata.
- Limit changes to `src/oracle/evm/native_token_bridge/GBridgeReceiver.sol` and the related unit test `test/unit/oracle/GBridgeReceiver.t.sol` to provide a minimal fix that preserves existing behavior and tests.

author: arcavenai
body:
## Summary

Implements the retrospector's BOARD.md recommendation pipeline as a Go package (`internal/retrospector/`), providing the unified output layer for SLAES's spec-chain and operational loops.

- **BoardWriter** (`board.go`): Parses existing BOARD.md to find the "Pending Recommendations" section, auto-assigns next P-NNN ID by scanning existing entries, and appends formatted recommendation rows matching the existing table format
- **Confidence scoring** (`confidence.go`): Applies the D-8 Watchmen safeguard rules — High (5+ data points across multiple PRs), Medium (2-4 data points), Low (1 data point). Includes `CountEvidenceForPattern` for flexible pattern matching against JSONL findings
- **Kill switch** (`killswitch.go`): Tracks recommendation outcomes (accepted/rejected/deferred), counts consecutive rejections, auto-triggers read-only mode after 3 consecutive rejections. State persists to JSON file, supports reset for recalibration
- **Batch pipeline** (`pipeline.go`): Cross-PR pattern detection for CI failures, merge conflicts, AC mismatches, and excessive rebasing. Produces ranked recommendations (highest confidence first), rate-limited to max 3 per batch cycle. Respects kill switch read-only state
- **Findings reader** (`findings.go`): JSONL findings log parser matching the schema defined in the retrospector agent definition (Story 51.1)

## Test Plan

- [x] 31 tests across 5 test files — all passing
- [x] Race detector clean (`go test -race`)
- [x] Zero lint warnings (`golangci-lint`)
- [x] Full test suite passes — no regressions (27 packages)
- [x] Table-driven tests for confidence scoring, ID generation, and formatting
- [x] Integration tests for BoardWriter (file I/O round-trip, ID increment verification)
- [x] Kill switch persistence test (write/reload from disk)
- [x] Pipeline rate-limiting test (max 3 recommendations per batch)
- [x] Pipeline read-only mode test (skip when kill switch triggered)
- [x] Pattern detection threshold tests (require minimum 2 data points)

## Files Changed

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `internal/retrospector/recommendation.go` | Core types: Recommendation, Confidence, Outcome |
| `internal/retrospector/board.go` | BOARD.md parser and writer |
| `internal/retrospector/confidence.go` | Confidence scoring and evidence counting |
| `internal/retrospector/killswitch.go` | Kill switch state management |
| `internal/retrospector/pipeline.go` | Batch analysis and pattern detection |
| `internal/retrospector/findings.go` | JSONL findings log reader |
| `internal/retrospector/*_test.go` | 31 tests across 5 test files |
| `docs/stories/51.6.story.md` | Story status → In Review |

## Opportunities (not implemented)

- CLI command (`threedoors retrospect`) to expose pipeline functionality for manual runs
- Integration with the retrospector agent's polling loop (Story 51.3 provides the data source)
- Recommendation deduplication (check if a similar recommendation already exists before filing)

author: rockfordlhotka
body:
## Summary

- **No results without accountId**: `get_calendar_events` and `list_calendars` were calling `GetAllAccountsAsync()` (which includes disabled accounts) when no `accountId` is specified. Disabled accounts silently return empty results from their providers, which could suppress events from enabled accounts. Switched to `GetEnabledAccounts()` so only active accounts are queried.
- **Date boundary quirk**: `endDate` was passed as midnight and used as an exclusive upper bound (`TimeMax`), so `endDate=2026-03-11` queried `< 2026-03-11T00:00:00Z` — missing the entire day. The tool now adds one day to an explicit `endDate`, making it inclusive. Callers no longer need to straddle the boundary (e.g. March 10–12 to get March 11 events).

## Test plan

- [ ] All 195 existing tests pass
- [ ] `get_calendar_events` without `accountId` returns events from all enabled accounts
- [ ] `get_calendar_events` with `startDate=endDate` (same day) returns events for that day
- [ ] `list_calendars` without `accountId` returns calendars from all enabled accounts

author: fjsuarez
body:
## Summary

Addresses #51 — late-year weather data gap caused by single-file ERA5 loading.

### Changes

**Loader** (`routetools/era5/loader.py`):
- `_normalize_time_coord()`: renames `time` → `valid_time` for consistent dimension naming across CDS and GCS sources
- `_load_datasets()`: opens one or more NetCDF files, normalizes time dims, concatenates along time axis
- `load_era5_windfield`, `load_era5_vectorfield`, `load_era5_wavefield`: accept `path: list[Path]` for multi-file concat + optional `voyage_hours` parameter that logs a warning when data coverage is insufficient

**Downloaders**:
- GCS (`download_gcs.py`): `_detect_time_dim()`, `_normalize_time_dim()`, `months` parameter, partial-year filenames
- CDS (`download_cds.py`): partial-year filename support

**CLI** (`scripts/download_era5.py`): `--months` flag forwarded to both backends

**Comparison script** (`scripts/compare_era5_sources.py`): downloads a subset from GCS and compares against existing CDS files, reporting grid alignment, NaN patterns, and value differences

**Dependencies**: added `gcsfs`, `zarr` for GCS access

### GCS vs CDS comparison results (Jan 2024 Atlantic)

| Field | Max abs diff | allclose(atol=1e-3) |
|-------|-------------|---------------------|
| u10   | 4.33e-04    | ✅ True             |
| v10   | 3.92e-04    | ✅ True             |
| swh   | 3.52e-04    | ✅ True             |
| mwd   | 1.06e-02    | ❌ False (0.01° max) |

Grids, timestamps, and NaN patterns are **identical**. Value differences are sub-1e-3 (float32 encoding differences between ARCO-ERA5 Zarr and CDS NetCDF pipelines).

### Tests
- 7 new tests: `valid_time` dim, multi-file concat, mixed dim concat, voyage coverage warning
- 921 total tests pass

Closes #51

author: theobhau183919-ux
body:
### Motivation
- Prevent validators from being forced into repeated quorum-certified JWK updates by an untrusted/externally-advanced relayer nonce for `gravity://` sources.
- Ensure updates are only produced when observed JWKS content actually differs from on-chain content, removing nonce-only triggering that can be abused for availability attacks.

### Description
- In `JWKManager::process_new_observation` (`crates/aptos-jwk-consensus/src/jwk_manager/mod.rs`) compute `jwks_changed = state.observed.as_ref() != state.on_chain.as_ref().map(ProviderJWKs::jwks)` and use it as part of the update decision.
- For gravity (oracle) observations (`observed_nonce = Some`), require both `jwks_changed` and `nonce > on_chain_version` to trigger an update instead of using the nonce comparison alone.
- For non-oracle observations (`observed_nonce = None`) retain the content-comparison behavior by using `jwks_changed` as the trigger.
- Add a regression test `test_gravity_nonce_alone_does_not_trigger_update` in `crates/aptos-jwk-consensus/src/jwk_manager/tests.rs` that verifies a very large relayer nonce alone does not start consensus when JWKS are unchanged.

### Testing
- Ran formatting with `cargo fmt` and `rustfmt` on the modified files successfully.
- Added the regression test `test_gravity_nonce_alone_does_not_trigger_update` and attempted a targeted run with `cargo test -p aptos-jwk-consensus test_gravity_nonce_alone_does_not_trigger_update -- --exact`, but the workspace compilation in this environment started and did not complete within the available run window, so the test could not be observed to finish here.
- Performed a `cargo check -p aptos-jwk-consensus --lib`/build attempts which began compiling workspace dependencies and emitted only existing warnings in this environment; final compilation/test completion was not reachable in the session.

author: clawrence-crabbot
body:
## Summary
Fixes a Discord reaction-routing gap where guild reaction events can be dropped when `guild_id` is present but the embedded `guild` object is missing.

Also adds explicit reaction-command system events for triage emojis so reaction-driven flows get deterministic intent payloads.

Closes #42601

## Changes
- `src/discord/monitor/listeners.ts`
  - Add guild resolution fallback by `data.guild_id` and wildcard `*` entry before early-return gate.
  - Emit explicit command system events for reaction add events:
    - ✅ → `accept`
    - ❌ → `reject`
    - 🔁 → `correct`
    - ✨ → `confirm`

## Why
In live Discord channels, triage reactions occasionally produced no action although `reactionNotifications` and allowlists were configured correctly. This was traced to reaction payloads that had `guild_id` but no embedded `guild`, causing the handler to return early.

## Validation
- Verified in a live Discord channel: reaction toggle now triggers triage flow again.
- Local static check performed by building patch against runtime bundles.

## Notes
- This PR keeps behavior channel-agnostic (no hardcoded guild/channel IDs).
- Fallback is only used when normal guild resolution fails.

author: ouankou
body:
## Summary

Fixes `ouankou/rex#387`.

- remove `test2018_73.C` from the disabled C++17 compile-test list so it runs as a normal CTest entry
- make `test2018_73.C` valid C++17 by including `<new>` for placement `new` / `std::launder`
- fix Clang frontend translation of `CXXNewExpr` initializers so `new T{...}` and other non-`CXXConstructExpr` initializers are preserved in the ROSE AST instead of being dropped

## Root Cause

The issue report correctly identified that `tests/nonsmoke/functional/CompileTests/Cxx17_tests/test2018_73.C` was missing `<new>`, but that was not the full current-tree failure.

After adding the missing header, REX still produced invalid output for:

```c++
new (&u.x) X{2};
```

The Clang frontend only populated `SgNewExp::constructor_args` from `CXXNewExpr::getConstructExpr()`. For aggregate/list initialization, LLVM 21 exposes the initializer through `CXXNewExpr::getInitializer()` as an `InitListExpr`, so the initializer was silently dropped and the unparser emitted `new (&u.x) X;`.

This change translates non-`CXXConstructExpr` new-expression initializers into a `SgConstructorInitializer` and preserves brace-initialization state, which fixes the real compiler bug instead of relying on a workaround.

## Validation

Ran with `build/lib` first in `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` to ensure the rebuilt in-tree libraries were used:

```bash
env LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/home/ouankou/Projects/rex-ai/rex-omp/build/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH \
  ctest --test-dir build --output-on-failure -j32 -R '^Cxx17_tests_test2018_73_C$'
```

Passed: `1/1`.

```bash
env LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/home/ouankou/Projects/rex-ai/rex-omp/build/lib:$LD_LIBRARY_PATH \
  ctest --test-dir build -R "rex|astInterface|testQuery|fortran|f90|f03|f77|caf|gfortran" \
    --exclude-regex "omp_lowering" --output-on-failure -j32
```

Passed: `4924/4924`.

Push hook suite also completed successfully on the final push:

```bash
ctest --test-dir build -R "rex|astInterface|testQuery|fortran|f90|f03|gfortran|OMPTEST_|OMPACCTEST_|OMPFORTRAN_|OMPVV_5_0_|OMPVV_4_5_|OMPVV_5_1_|OMPVV_5_2_|OMPVV_6_0_|omp_lowering_|OMPLOWERING_CPU_|OMPLOWERING_RODINIA_"

author: sayayai
body:
The `LogWatcher` in `vrmemoir` was performing several sub-optimal operations in its hot path. This PR implements targeted optimizations to reduce its resource footprint:

1. **Efficient File Selection**: Switched from `sort_by` to `max_by_key` when finding the latest log file. This reduces the complexity from $O(N \log N)$ to $O(N)$, which is significant as the number of log files in the VRChat directory grows over time.
2. **Aggressive Log Filtering**: VRChat logs are extremely noisy. By adding an early return check for `[Behaviour]` or `uSpeak` keywords in `parse_line`, we now bypass expensive regex checks and string operations for the vast majority of log entries.
3. **Lazy Timestamp Parsing**: Timestamps are now parsed via a closure only when a relevant log event is confirmed, further reducing CPU cycles on irrelevant lines.
4. **Memory Allocation Reduction**: In `read_new_lines`, we no longer collect lines into an intermediate `Vec<&str>`. Instead, we process them using a `peekable` iterator, which avoids heap allocations for every read cycle and correctly handles incomplete trailing lines.

Verification:
- Added `tests::test_parse_line_optim` in `src/watcher.rs`.
- Ran `cargo test`, all tests passed.
- Verified manual冒烟测试(smoke check) would be unaffected as core event detection logic is preserved.

## Summary

Recovers the eval system from commit `baa6035` (originally on `feat/generator-eval-blocks` branch, never merged to main due to PR #8 targeting the wrong base branch).

- Adds in-process code evaluation via `eval` terminal modifier — JavaScript blocks execute in a shared VM context with Effection APIs, bindings shared across blocks within a component, and full journal support via `durableEval`
- Adds `persist` modifier — extends resource lifetime from block scope to component's eval scope via context flag pattern
- Adds `timeout` modifier — constrains block execution time using `@effectionx/timebox`
- Creates shared eval infrastructure: `EvalEnvCtx` (binding environment), `EvalScopeCtx` (eval scope), `EvalCtxKey` (VM context), `PersistFlagCtx` (persist flag)
- Eval scope created before `durableRun` to ensure channel processor reachability

## New files

**Source (6):** `src/eval-transform.ts`, `src/eval-context.ts`, `src/eval-env.ts`, `src/eval-handler.ts`, `src/modifiers/persist.ts`, `src/modifiers/timeout.ts`

**Tests (9):** Transform (16 tests), VM context (8), Bindings (5), DurableEval integration (6), Middleware conformance (7), Persist (7), Eval scope (2), Staleness (5), Timeout (6)

`@effectionx/converge`, `@effectionx/scope-eval`, `@effectionx/timebox`, `acorn`, `magic-string`

Adds a new method and supporting FFI types to expose the current execution state of all registered migration processors.

## Changes
- `MigrationController::list_all_record`s — returns a Vec<MigrationRecordEntry> with one entry per registered processor. Acquires the migration lock for a consistent snapshot. Processors
  with no persisted record appear with NotStarted and zero attempts; corrupted or missing store entries are treated as resets rather than errors.
- `MigrationRecordEntry (uniffi::Record)` — FFI-facing DTO that combines migration_id (not present on MigrationRecord itself) with the externally relevant fields from the persisted
  record. 
- `MigrationStatus` — derives uniffi::Enum so it can be used in the new FFI record.
- `mod.rs` — exports MigrationRecordEntry as part of the public API.

### Motivation
- A recent change allowed an attacker to supply an arbitrary `peer_id` in the client prologue under `HandshakeAuthMode::MaybeMutual` and bypass the binding between the reported `peer_id` and the authenticated static public key, enabling peer_id spoofing and connection replacement.
- Restore the original security invariant that the peer_id must be derivable from the remote Noise static key for all inbound connections, even when the peer is not in the trusted set.

### Description
- In `network/framework/src/noise/handshake.rs` (inbound path for `HandshakeAuthMode::MaybeMutual`) derive the peer id from the authenticated remote static key via `aptos_types::account_address::from_identity_public_key(remote_public_key)` and compare it to the self-reported `remote_peer_id` from the prologue. 
- If the derived peer id does not match the prologue `peer_id`, return `NoiseHandshakeError::ClientPeerIdMismatch`; otherwise preserve the existing role-inference behavior unchanged.
- This is a minimal change localized to the MaybeMutual non-trusted branch and keeps mutual-authenticated behavior intact.

### Testing
- Ran an attempted test with the wrong package name: `cargo test -p network-framework noise::handshake::test_handshake_client_peerid_mismatch_fails_server_only_auth -- --nocapture`, which failed because the package name did not match (expected failure due to invocation target mismatch).

author: swain
body:
## Summary

- Raw SQL queries in `people.service.ts` were casting state values to `"public"."USState"`, but the `Voter` and `DistrictVoter` tables live in the `green` schema
- This type mismatch prevents PostgreSQL from using indexes on the `State` columns, forcing a full sequential scan on every `COUNT(*)` query
- The COUNT query was taking **~3,900–4,010ms** per request, making `POST /v1/people` consistently slow

**Root cause traces:**
- [people-api trace 595a027](https://goodparty.grafana.net/explore?schemaVersion=1&panes=%7B%22a%22%3A%7B%22datasource%22%3A%22grafanacloud-traces%22%2C%22queries%22%3A%5B%7B%22refId%22%3A%22A%22%2C%22query%22%3A%22595a027113c279a2fe7beb2c46afc22d%22%2C%22datasource%22%3A%7B%22type%22%3A%22tempo%22%2C%22uid%22%3A%22grafanacloud-traces%22%7D%7D%5D%7D%7D) — COUNT took 3905ms
- [people-api trace 918a8f4](https://goodparty.grafana.net/explore?schemaVersion=1&panes=%7B%22a%22%3A%7B%22datasource%22%3A%22grafanacloud-traces%22%2C%22queries%22%3A%5B%7B%22refId%22%3A%22A%22%2C%22query%22%3A%22918a8f470fc5e623671d37d083b93132%22%2C%22datasource%22%3A%7B%22type%22%3A%22tempo%22%2C%22uid%22%3A%22grafanacloud-traces%22%7D%7D%5D%7D%7D) — COUNT took 4010ms

**Fix:** Change all `CAST(... AS "public"."USState")` → `CAST(... AS "green"."USState")` in `rawBuildWhere` and `getById` (3 occurrences in `people.service.ts`).

## Test plan

- [ ] Deploy to QA and run `POST /v1/people` with a district filter — confirm p95 latency drops significantly
- [ ] Verify `GET /v1/contacts` in gp-api also recovers (it was blocked on this call)
- [ ] Check that state filtering still returns correct results (no regression in data)

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches raw SQL used by `GET /people` and count queries; while change is small, it can affect query results and performance if the enum/schema differs across environments.
> 
> **Overview**
> Updates `PeopleService` raw SQL to cast state values to `"green"."USState"` (instead of `"public"."USState"`) in both `findPerson` and `rawBuildWhere`.
> 
> This aligns the cast type with the `green`-schema tables (`Voter`/`DistrictVoter`), avoiding type mismatches that can prevent index usage on `State`-filtered queries.

body:
Gallery and booking pages load slowly due to uncompressed API responses, eager image loading, and no HTTP caching on the public album endpoint. ## Changes - **Gzip compression** (`server/index.js`, `server/package.json`): Added `compression` middleware as the first Express middleware after CORS. Reduces JSON/JS/CSS payload sizes ~70–90% — the biggest single win for large album responses. ```js app.use(cors()); app.use(compression()); // ← new ``` - **Native lazy image loading** (`src/components/ProgressiveImg.tsx`): Added `loading="lazy" decoding="async"` to the thumbnail ``. Prevents the browser from firing dozens of parallel image requests on initial render; images load only as they scroll into view. - **HTTP caching for public album endpoint** (`server/index.js`): Added `Cache-Control: public, max-age=60, stale-while-revalidate=300` to `/api/public-album/:albumSlug`. Previously every visit (including back-navigation) hit the server cold. Extracted a `SHORT_CACHE` constant shared with the already-cached `/api/tenant/:slug/public` endpoint.

author: copilot
body:
Tests broke after PR #4 replaced Ghostscript with PDFtoImage/SkiaSharp due to a combination of framework mismatch, stream lifecycle bugs, and a placeholder test that called into broken code paths.

## Root causes

- **`net7.0` unavailable in CI** — both projects and both workflows pinned to an EOL SDK
- **`Convert("")` opened a directory as a file** — `Path.Combine(tempDir, "")` resolves to the temp dir itself; `File.OpenRead` on a directory throws `UnauthorizedAccessException`
- **`GetPageCount` closes the stream** — the loop then reset `stream.Position = 0` on a disposed stream → `ObjectDisposedException`
- **Images written to CWD** — `ConvertToImages` used a bare filename (`{name}_page1.png`) instead of writing to `_path.GetTempPath()`

## Changes

- **Framework / CI**: `net7.0` → `net8.0` in both `.csproj` files and both workflow files
- **`PdfToImageService.ConvertToImages`**: open a separate stream per page (avoids disposed-stream error); write output PNGs under `_path.GetTempPath()`
  ```csharp
  // Before: reused a stream that GetPageCount had already closed
  using var stream = File.OpenRead(pdfFilePath);
  int pageCount = Conversion.GetPageCount(stream); // closes stream
  for (int i = 0; i < pageCount; i++) {
      stream.Position = 0; // ObjectDisposedException
      ...
  }

  // After: fresh stream per page
  using (var countStream = File.OpenRead(pdfFilePath))
      pageCount = Conversion.GetPageCount(countStream);
  for (int i = 0; i < pageCount; i++) {
      using var stream = File.OpenRead(pdfFilePath);
      ...
  }
  ```
- **`SmpleTests`**: replaced the broken `Convert("")` smoke test with:
  - `SimpleTest` — asserts both services are constructed without error
  - `ConvertToImages_WithValidPdf_ReturnsImagePaths` — writes a minimal valid PDF to the temp dir, converts it, asserts the output PNG exists on disk
  - `TearDown` — cleans up generated PNG/PDF files from the temp dir after each test

### Motivation
- Prevent a liveness/DoS vector where unbounded `networkAddresses`/`fullnodeAddresses` blobs are stored and emitted in `NewEpochEvent`, which can bloat event payloads and cause epoch transitions to revert due to gas exhaustion.
- Preserve current functionality while adding minimal, explicit validation to keep validator metadata bounded and predictable.

### Description
- Add two new explicit errors `NetworkAddressesTooLong` and `FullnodeAddressesTooLong` in `src/foundation/Errors.sol` to surface oversized-blob failures.
- Introduce `MAX_NETWORK_ADDRESSES_LENGTH` and `MAX_FULLNODE_ADDRESSES_LENGTH` (both `256` bytes) in `src/staking/ValidatorManagement.sol` and enforce these limits in the genesis initialization path (`_initializeGenesisValidator`).
- Enforce the same bounds during runtime registration by extending `_validateRegistration` to accept and validate `networkAddresses` and `fullnodeAddresses` and updating `registerValidator` to pass the blobs through validation; storage of the blobs remains unchanged when within limits.
- Add unit tests in `test/unit/staking/ValidatorManagement.t.sol` to assert `registerValidator` reverts when either blob exceeds the configured limit.

### Testing
- Added targeted unit tests (`test/unit/staking/ValidatorManagement.t.sol`) that assert reverts for oversized `networkAddresses` and `fullnodeAddresses` during `registerValidator` (tests added but not executed here).
- Attempted to run `forge test --match-test registerValidator`, but `forge` is not installed in the environment so tests could not be executed (no test run results available).
- All changes are minimal and localized to validation paths to preserve existing behavior when inputs are within bounds.

author: turnerinnovate
body:
### Motivation
- Provide a producible scaffold for a two-product system (AI Coaching / Tournament Judging) with shared analysis primitives and clear separation of responsibilities. 
- Offer local development ergonomics (Docker Compose, demo `index.html`, `.env.example`) and CI validation for the analysis service.
- Introduce deterministic scoring, rules, and judging primitives to centralize rubric/deduction logic and provenance.
- Seed a minimal DB schema and example data to accelerate local demos and integration work.

### Description
- Add a Next.js `apps/web` app with basic pages and REST-style API routes for `health`, `judge`, `tournament`, and `training`, plus `next.config.js`, `package.json`, and TypeScript config. 
- Add an analysis microservice `services/analysis` implemented with FastAPI, including `/analyze` and `/health` endpoints, Dockerfile, requirements, and unit tests. 
- Add a Python `services/worker` with job primitives, scoring/analysis orchestration logic, and unit tests for job processing behavior. 
- Add shared TypeScript packages implementing core algorithms and domain logic: `packages/analysis` (DTW), `packages/judging`, `packages/rules-engine`, `packages/scoring`, `packages/storage`, and `packages/types`. 
- Add Prisma schema, placeholder migration, and `prisma/seed.ts` to define DB models and seed demo data. 
- Add developer conveniences: `Docker Compose` for local services, root `package.json` workspaces, `.env.example`, `README.md`, `docs/architecture.md`, `index.html` standalone demo, and `scripts/setup.sh`. 
- Add GitHub Actions CI workflow `/.github/workflows/ci.yml` that sets up Python and runs analysis service tests. 

### Testing
- Ran `python -m pytest services/analysis/tests` which executed the FastAPI analysis service tests and verified `/health` and `/analyze` behavior (tests passed). 
- Ran unit tests for the worker with `python -m pytest services/worker/tests` which validated scoring decisions, review gating, and failure handling (tests passed). 
- CI pipeline added to run `python -m pytest services/analysis/tests` on push and pull requests to keep analysis regressions guarded (configured to run on `ubuntu-latest`).

author: shonfeder
body: Fast, portable, and opinionated build system - Project page: https://github.com/ocaml/dune - Documentation: https://dune.readthedocs.io/ ##### CHANGES: ### Fixed - `Dyn.to_string` now uses a smarter way to convert floats. This ensures that floats are printed with enough precision to round-trip and are valid OCaml lexemes. (ocaml/dune#12982, fixes ocaml/dune#12980, @Alizter) - Fix `dune install --prefix` failing with relative paths outside the workspace like `../foo` (ocaml/dune#12993, fixes ocaml/dune#12241, @benodiwal) - Place the default trace file inside the build directory at the workspace root, rather than relative to the current directory. (ocaml/dune#13735, @vouillon) - Fixed interpreting relative paths in `%{bin:..}` and `%{bin-available:..}`. These are now interpreted correctly, relative to the dune file they're in. (ocaml/dune#13712, fixes ocaml/dune#9564, @anmonteiro) - Delete sandboxes with broken permissions (ocaml/dune#13511, @rgrinberg) - Fix compiling Menhir parsers that refer to sibling modules within a subdirectory of `(include_subdirs qualified)`. (ocaml/dune#13118, fixes ocaml/dune#11119, @anmonteiro) - Fixed the dependency specification of C stubs, which could result in C stubs not getting rebuilt when needed (which could in turn lead to segmentation faults and other hard-to-track bugs). (ocaml/dune#13652, fixes ocaml/dune#13651, @nojb) - Fix the Dune cache on Windows by correctly handling renames onto read-only files. Before this change, the Dune cache would be filled but the stored artifacts would not generally be usable by Dune. (ocaml/dune#13713, @Nevor) - Fix rpc not transferring promotion warnings to the client (ocaml/dune#12604, fixes ocaml/dune#12578, @ElectreAAS) - Fix issue where `dune exec -w` was unable to kill running programs on rebuild. (ocaml/dune#12360, fixes ocaml/dune#12323, @Alizter) - Fix package extraction on systems with tar implementations that don't auto-detect compression (e.g., OpenBSD). Dune now passes explicit decompression flags (-z for gzip, -j for bzip2) when needed, and provides clear error messages for unsupported formats like XZ and LZMA. (ocaml/dune#13688, fixes ocaml/dune#10123, @Alizter) - Resolve context and workspace binaries introduced by the respective `(env (binaries ..))` stanzas. (ocaml/dune#12952, fixes ocaml/dune#6220, @anmonteiro) - Fix `diff` promotions originating from sandboxed rules. Previously, they would be completely ignored as the sandbox with the promoted file would be destroyed if the promotion fired (ocaml/dune#13520, @rgrinberg) - Fix failure to digest installed directory targets, allowing them to be used as dependencies to other rules. (ocaml/dune#13045, @anmonteiro) - Fix handling of `(select ..)` field when used with `(include_subdirs ..)`. `(select from ..)` modules now parse `path` as a relative path starting from the module group root (ocaml/dune#13175, fixes ocaml/dune#4383, ocaml/dune#12450, @anmonteiro) - Fix dune trying to kill processes that were already reaped due to race conditions (ocaml/dune#13245, @rgrinberg) - Add `O_CLOEXEC` to all files used for stdin/stdout/stderr (ocaml/dune#13385, @rgrinberg) - Fix `$ dune promote dir/foo` when `dir` does not exist (ocaml/dune#13493, @rgrinberg) - Fix `(select ..)` field evaluation when a transitive library has optional dependencies (fixes ocaml/dune#13299, ocaml/dune#13389, @anmonteiro) - Fix sandboxed builds of `library` stanzas that set `(stdlib (modules_before_stdlib ..))` (ocaml/dune#13624, @anmonteiro) - Dune cache: use of hard links under Windows. (ocaml/dune#13714, @Nevor) - Fixed non-build caches not following `$DUNE_CACHE_ROOT` and instead only relying on `$XDG_CACHE_HOME`. This means the normal build cache moves: `$DUNE_CACHE_ROOT -> $DUNE_CACHE_ROOT/db` (no changes if that variable was unset). Affected users can prevent a full cache invalidation by moving previous contents: `cd $DUNE_CACHE_ROOT; mkdir db; mv db`. (ocaml/dune#11612, fixes ocaml/dune#11584, @ElectreAAS) - `$ dune promotion list` writes output to stdout rather than stderr (ocaml/dune#13462) - Improve handling of empty files in the `diff` action. These are now correctly distinguished from *empty* files. (ocaml/dune#13696, @rgrinberg) - Pass `/dev/null` to `--diff-command` instead of non-existent files (ocaml/dune#13696, @rgrinberg) - Fix failure when multiple `rocq.extraction` stanzas existing in a directory (ocaml/dune#13531, fixes ocaml/dune#8042, @rlepigre-skylabs-ai) - Print `$ dune promotion show` output to stdout rather than stderr (ocaml/dune#13481, @rgrinberg) - Fix deadlock in the `memo` library in the presence of dependency cycles (ocaml/dune#13625, @anmonteiro) - Fix promotions that modify a directory into a file (ocaml/dune#13516, fixes ocaml/dune#4067, @rgrinberg) - Fix installation of implementations of virtual libraries. This failed when the implementation had no private modules, but the virtual library did (ocaml/dune#10635, @rgrinberg) - Respect the `(dir ..)` field on packages when setting up cram tests (ocaml/dune#13581, @rgrinberg) ### Added - Add support for generating `.cms` files using oxcaml and adding `.cms` or `.cmt` files as compilation dependencies (ocaml/dune#13397, @spiessimon) - Add trace events for custom actions (ocaml/dune#13265, @rgrinberg) - Allow enabling extensions with `(using ..)` in `dune-workspace` files (ocaml/dune#13395, @spiessimon) - Add sandbox extraction trace event (ocaml/dune#13544, @rgrinberg) - Add the initial cwd to the first config event (ocaml/dune#13026, @rgrinberg) - Dune dune produces trace events in `DUNE_ACTION_TRACE_DIR` if this variable is set. (ocaml/dune#13302, @rgrinberg) - Add file watching events to the trace file (ocaml/dune#13038, @rgrinberg) - Introduce the `$ dune trace cat` subcommand to view the trace file. (ocaml/dune#13055, @rgrinberg) - Add diagnostic events to the trace. (ocaml/dune#13041, @rgrinberg) - Add `DUNE_JOBS` environment variable for controlling concurrency of Dune from environment. The `INSIDE_DUNE` variable also now no longer controls concurrency (ocaml/dune#12800, @Alizter) - Support for Rocq expected output tests (ocaml/dune#13632, @rlepigre-skylabs-ai) - Add `rusage` information to completed processes in the trace (@rgrinberg, ocaml/dune#13241) - Add process start events to the trace (ocaml/dune#13261, rgrinberg) - Generate odoc documentation in markdown using the `@doc-markdown` alias (ocaml/dune#12581, @davesnx) - Add timing information for every command executed by cram (ocaml/dune#13092, @rgrinberg) - Add the workspace root to the config trace event (ocaml/dune#12922, @rgrinberg) - Introduce the `dune-action-trace` library. This public library is to be used by custom actions to emit trace events while executed as part of a dune build. The trace events emitted through this library will be incorporated into dune's own trace (ocaml/dune#13348, @rgrinberg) - Add `dune-find-dominating` to `dune.el`, a command to find the dominating dune file. (ocaml/dune#12696, @arvidj) - Add a `--no-recursive` flag to `$ dune describe workspace` (ocaml/dune#13590, @rgrinberg) - Trace events for files written directly by dune (ocaml/dune#13618, @rgrinberg) - Allow expansion of special forms like `(:include ..)` and `%{read-lines:..}` in the `modules` specification for the `ocamllex`, `ocamlyacc` and `menhir` stanzas. (ocaml/dune#13105, ocaml/dune#13135, ocaml/dune#13157, @anmonteiro) - Add a trace event for snapshotting the asndbox (ocaml/dune#13541, @rgrinberg) - Add signal send and receive events to the trace (ocaml/dune#13193, @rgrinberg) - Emit final trace event before exiting. (ocaml/dune#13018, @rgrinberg) - `dune runtest` can now run individual test executables from

author: copilot
body:
Introduces **Flowie**: an optional private GitHub repository that stores the user's research profile (stances, writing style, methodological preferences, key beliefs), enabling Claude to personalize assistance across all neuroflow phases.

## New files

- **`commands/flowie.md`** — `/flowie` command with five modes:
  - `--init` — interview-driven profile creation; writes `profile.md`, `ideas.md`, `sync.json` under `.neuroflow/.flowie/`
  - `--sync` — pull-before-push GitHub sync via `gh` CLI or PAT; diffs shown before applying; merge conflicts handled side-by-side; staging clone in `.neuroflow/.flowie/.remote-sync` (cleaned up after)
  - `--link` — writes a `flowie_profile` reference into the current project's `project_config.md`
  - `--view` — read-only profile display
  - `--identify` — synthesizes existing profile data into a 4–6 sentence "who you are" paragraph; requires user confirmation before writing

- **`skills/phase-flowie/SKILL.md`** — defines how Claude reads and applies the profile silently across all phases (ideation, paper-write, data-analyze, etc.); enforces diff-before-write and pull-before-push rules; privacy rules excluding profile data from external-facing outputs

- **`agents/flowie.md`** — autonomous personalization agent; reads profile at session start; surfaces stances/preferences contextually; offers a sync reminder when `last_synced` exceeds 7 days (documented rationale: frequent enough to stay current, infrequent enough to avoid notification fatigue)

- **`docs/commands/flowie.md`** — user-facing docs covering prerequisites (GitHub account + PAT or `gh` CLI), all five modes, privacy model, and sync behavior

## Updated files

- `README.md` — `## What's new in 0.1.8` section; `/flowie` added to Utility Commands table; `neuroflow:phase-flowie` added to Skills table; `flowie` added to Agents table
- `mkdocs.yml` — flowie entries under Commands (Utilities) and Skills (Phases) nav; `extra.version` bumped to `"0.1.8"`
- `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` — version `0.1.7` → `0.1.8`

## Privacy model

Profile data lives in a private GitHub repo. It is excluded from `/export` by default and never surfaced in external-facing documents (papers, reports). PATs are held in memory only — never written to disk.

body:
Scaffolds the full CRYPTRAC (National Crypto Transaction Monitoring & Tax Compliance System) on top of the existing Express/TypeScript skeleton. All services use in-memory stores so the project compiles and tests run without a database.

## Core Types & Validation
- `src/types/index.ts` — enums (`TransactionType`, `RiskLevel`, `ComplianceStatus`, `ReportType`, `UserRole`, `TaxEventType`) and all domain interfaces
- `src/validators/schemas.ts` — Zod schemas for transactions, wallets, and auth with inferred TS types

## Middleware
- `src/middleware/auth.ts` — JWT `authenticate` + `authorize(...roles)` RBAC factory; extends `Express.Request` with `user: JwtPayload`
- `src/middleware/validate.ts` — generic Zod middleware targeting `body | query | params`
- `src/middleware/rateLimiter.ts` — custom IP-based sliding-window rate limiter (10 req/min auth, 100 req/min API, 30 req/min compliance); no external dependency required

## Services
- **`auth.service`** — bcrypt registration, JWT login/verify
- **`transaction.service`** — CRUD + automated risk scoring (amount thresholds, sanctions address matching, structuring heuristics)
- **`compliance.service`** — SAR (≥ $10k), CTR (≥ $10k), FATF Recommendation 16 Travel Rule (≥ $1k)
- **`wallet.service`** — registry with risk scoring and sanctions list screening
- **`tax.service`** — FIFO cost basis, capital gains classification (short/long-term), income events (mining, staking, airdrop)

## Routes
Four route modules wired into the existing `src/index.ts` mounts: `/auth`, `/transactions`, `/compliance`, `/wallets` — all authenticated via `authenticate`, sensitive actions gated by `authorize`.

## Database
`prisma/schema.prisma` defines `User`, `Transaction`, `Wallet`, `ComplianceReport`, `TaxEvent`, `TravelRuleData` with appropriate relations and indexes.

## Tests
44 tests across two suites:
- `compliance.service.test.ts` — SAR/CTR threshold detection, Travel Rule threshold, multi-report generation
- `tax.service.test.ts` — FIFO ordering across lots, short vs. long-term gain classification, income event types, tax summary aggregation

## Context

The repository `ssahmadtijani/CRYPTRAC` is a **Crypto Transaction Reporting and Compliance System (NCTMTCS)** aligned with FATF Recommendation 16 (Travel Rule) and AML/CFT Standards. It currently has only:
- `README.md` (basic description)
- `package.json` (dependencies already defined)
- `tsconfig.json`, `.gitignore`, `.env.example`, `jest.config.js`
- `src/index.ts` (Express server entry point)
- `src/utils/logger.ts` (Winston logger)
- `src/middleware/errorHandler.ts` and `src/middleware/requestLogger.ts`

## Task

Scaffold the complete remaining project structure. All files below must be created. The project uses **TypeScript, Express, Prisma, Zod, ethers.js, Winston, JWT (jsonwebtoken), and bcryptjs** — all already in `package.json`.

### 1. Core Type Definitions — `src/types/index.ts`

Create comprehensive type definitions including:
- **Enums**: `TransactionType` (TRANSFER, TRADE, DEPOSIT, WITHDRAWAL, SWAP, STAKING, MINING, AIRDROP), `RiskLevel` (LOW, MEDIUM, HIGH, CRITICAL), `ComplianceStatus` (PENDING, APPROVED, FLAGGED, REJECTED, UNDER_REVIEW), `ReportType` (SAR, CTR, TRAVEL_RULE, TAX_SUMMARY), `UserRole` (ADMIN, COMPLIANCE_OFFICER, ANALYST, AUDITOR, USER), `TaxEventType` (CAPITAL_GAIN_SHORT, CAPITAL_GAIN_LONG, INCOME, MINING_INCOME, STAKING_REWARD, AIRDROP_INCOME)
- **Interfaces**: `Transaction`, `Wallet`, `ComplianceReport`, `TaxEvent`, `TravelRuleData`, `User`, `ApiResponse<T>`, `PaginationParams`, `TransactionFilter`, `TaxSummary`

### 2. Zod Validation Schemas — `src/validators/schemas.ts`

Create Zod schemas for:
- `createTransactionSchema` — validates transaction creation input
- `transactionFilterSchema` — validates query/filter params with pagination
- `walletSchema` — validates wallet creation
- `loginSchema` and `registerSchema` — validates auth input
- Export inferred TypeScript types from each schema

### 3. Auth Middleware — `src/middleware/auth.ts`

- JWT token verification middleware (`authenticate`)
- Role-based authorization middleware (`authorize(...roles)`)
- Extends Express `Request` type to include `user` property

### 4. Validation Middleware — `src/middleware/validate.ts`

- Generic Zod validation middleware that validates `req.body`, `req.query`, or `req.params`
- Returns structured error responses on validation failure

### 5. Services

#### `src/services/transaction.service.ts`
- `createTransaction(data)` — creates and stores a transaction, auto-triggers risk assessment
- `getTransactions(filter)` — paginated, filtered transaction listing
- `getTransactionById(id)` — single transaction lookup
- `assessTransactionRisk(transaction)` — risk scoring logic based on amount thresholds, sanctioned addresses, etc.

#### `src/services/compliance.service.ts`
- `checkCompliance(transaction)` — runs compliance checks (SAR threshold $10,000, CTR threshold $10,000, Travel Rule threshold $1,000)
- `generateSAR(transaction)` — generates Suspicious Activity Report
- `generateCTR(transaction)` — generates Currency Transaction Report
- `checkTravelRule(transaction)` — checks and generates Travel Rule data per FATF Rec 16
- `getComplianceReports(filter)` — paginated report listing

#### `src/services/wallet.service.ts`
- `registerWallet(data)` — registers a wallet with risk scoring
- `getWalletByAddress(address)` — lookup
- `updateWalletRiskScore(address)` — recalculates risk score
- `checkSanctionsList(address)` — checks against sanctioned addresses (stub/mock)

#### `src/services/tax.service.ts`
- `calculateTaxEvents(userId, taxYear)` — calculates capital gains/losses using FIFO method
- `generateTaxSummary(userId, taxYear)` — aggregates tax events into a summary
- `classifyTaxEvent(transaction)` — determines tax event type (short/long term gains, income, etc.)
- `calculateCostBasis(asset, amount, method)` — cost basis calculation (FIFO default)

#### `src/services/auth.service.ts`
- `register(data)` — user registration with bcrypt password hashing
- `login(data)` — authentication returning JWT token
- `generateToken(user)` — JWT token generation
- `verifyToken(token)` — JWT token verification

### 6. Routes

#### `src/routes/auth.routes.ts`
- `POST /register` — user registration
- `POST /login` — user login

#### `src/routes/transaction.routes.ts`
- `POST /` — create transaction (authenticated)
- `GET /` — list transactions with filters (authenticated)
- `GET /:id` — get transaction by ID (authenticated)
- `POST /:id/assess` — trigger risk assessment (compliance officer+)

#### `src/routes/compliance.routes.ts`
- `POST /check/:transactionId` — run compliance check (compliance officer+)
- `GET /reports` — list compliance reports (authenticated)
- `GET /reports/:id` — get report by ID (authenticated)
- `POST /sar/:transactionId` — generate SAR (compliance officer+)
- `POST /travel-rule/:transactionId` — check travel rule (compliance officer+)

#### `src/routes/wallet.routes.ts`
- `POST /` — register wallet (authenticated)
- `GET /:address` — get wallet info (authenticated)
-...

author: thomas-waite
body:
## Add `sync_backup()`, to allow for a first time backup upload before vault mutations
When a user first creates a backup in a host app, it's an explicit action taken by a user to make a backup. It is not in response to a vault mutation. So, we need a method that can force a backup of the vault to be made if the host app needs one.

Added `sync_backup()` to do this. Also done a slight refactor of the internal logic to propagate errors, similar to how the existing backup system works.



<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Touches core credential storage synchronization by replacing `std::sync::Mutex` with `parking_lot::Mutex` and removing poison-error handling, which could affect concurrency behavior. Adds a new backup-trigger path (`sync_backup`) that exports plaintext vault snapshots on demand, so backup integrations should be revalidated.
> 
> **Overview**
> Adds `CredentialStore::sync_backup()` to explicitly export the current vault and invoke the registered `WalletKitBackupManager::on_vault_changed` callback even when no vault mutation occurred (e.g., first-time backup setup), with new tests covering empty and non-empty vault cases.
> 
> Refactors storage locking to use `parking_lot::Mutex` (new optional dependency under the `storage` feature), simplifying APIs by removing `Result` from `storage_paths`/`paths` and eliminating poisoned-lock error paths; related authenticator tests and integration tests are updated accordingly. Backup export/callback failures remain best-effort and are now more explicitly logged/documented as non-propagated.
>

body:
### Motivation
- The `useCompanyCards(companyId, contactId?)` hook accepted `contactId` but ignored it, causing incorrect caching and query results.
- Calls that invalidate `['company_cards', id]` should clear all contact-specific variants, so cache-key strategy must support contact-scoped entries.
- Preserve existing behavior of returning a single row for the (company, contact) pair while enabling contact-scoped caching.

### Description
- Updated the query key to include the contact parameter as `queryKey: ["company_cards", companyId, contactId ?? null]` so each contact variant is cached separately.
- Changed the Supabase query to filter by both `company_id` and `contact_id` when `contactId` is provided (`.eq("company_id", companyId!).eq("contact_id", contactId)`) and to target company-scoped rows when not provided (`.eq("company_id", companyId!).is("contact_id", null)`), while keeping `.maybeSingle()`.
- Verified existing invalidation sites already use prefix invalidation (`exact: false`) to clear all `['company_cards', id, contactId]` variants, so no further changes to invalidation calls were necessary.

### Testing
- Ran a repository search for `invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ["company_cards", id] })` to confirm callsites, and the search found the expected usages (succeeded).
- Ran `npm run lint -- src/hooks/useSupabase.ts` to validate formatting and lint rules, but ESLint failed to run in this environment due to a missing dev dependency (`@eslint/js`), so linting could not be completed (failed).

the requirements below.

<!-- ** Please select "Allow edits from maintainers" in the PR Options ** -->

## Motivation

<!--
Explain the context and why you're making that change. What is the problem
you're trying to solve? In some cases there is not a problem and this can be
thought of as being the motivation for your change.
-->

Closes #13334

`forge fmt` currently enforces same-line opening braces, so users cannot preserve Allman-style block formatting. Allman style could be convenient for former C devs. 

## Solution

<!--
Summarize the solution and provide any necessary context needed to understand
the code change.
-->

Add a new `[fmt]` config option, `brace_style`, with support for `same_line` and `allman`.

While the original request mentioned a flag, this is implemented as a `foundry.toml` formatter option to match the existing formatter configuration model in Foundry.

The implementation keeps the default behavior unchanged and applies brace-style selection across Solidity and Yul block formatting. It only affects block braces and does not change delimiter braces such as import lists or named arguments.

This feature touches several formatter paths because brace placement is currently distributed across multiple formatting entry points. That is still reasonable for the current scope, but if the formatter style system becomes more complex, this part of the architecture should be revisited.

## How to use

In `foundry.toml`:

```toml
[fmt]
brace_style = "allman" // same_line by default
```

Then run:

```forge fmt```

or:

```forge fmt --check```

body:
### Motivation

- Advance the active `scheduler / threads` milestone by introducing deterministic per-thread context save/restore contracts so scheduler handoff paths can be modeled and tested end-to-end.
- Provide canonical transcript lines and host-side helpers to make context handoff observable and verifiable in unit tests, UEFI boot transcripts, and smoke checks.

### Description

- Add canonical boot transcript strings and byte accessors for thread context save/restore (`thread ctx save` / `thread ctx restore`) in `kernel/src/lib.rs` and expose them to firmware via `boot/uefi-entry` accessors. 
- Introduce `EarlyThreadContext`, `EarlyThreadContextHandoffReport`, `EarlyThreadContextHandoffError`, and the helper `model_early_thread_context_handoff` to produce deterministic saved/restored RIP/RSP snapshots from modeled scheduler state. 
- Wire the context-handoff transcript into the UEFI boot flow (`run_entry`) so save/restore lines are emitted between the scheduler round-robin selection and thread dequeue, and add corresponding message accessors in `boot/uefi-entry/src/lib.rs`. 
- Extend unit tests in both `kernel` and `uefi-entry` to validate the new canonical lines, handoff report values, and VGA transcript ordering, and update `tools/smoke-test.sh` to require the new context lines in both source and (optional) QEMU serial checks; update `docs/status/current.md` to record the completed slice and next target.

author: xxczaki
body:
## Problem

`~/.claude/` lives on the `home` emptyDir volume, so Claude Code's config (`.config.json`, `settings.json`) is lost on every pod restart. This means:
- Onboarding wizard may re-trigger
- Trust dialogs for project directories need re-accepting
- API key rejection config is lost (risking use of shared ANTHROPIC_API_KEY instead of the subscription OAuth token)
- Dangerous mode permission prompt reappears

Previously this was handled via a workspace script (`scripts/setup-claude-code.sh`) triggered from HEARTBEAT.md, but heartbeat is now disabled.

## Solution

Add a `setup-claude-code-config` init container that runs after `install-claude-code`. It:
1. Seeds `~/.claude/.config.json` — skips onboarding, trusts project dirs, rejects ANTHROPIC_API_KEY
2. Seeds `~/.claude/settings.json` — skips dangerous mode permission prompt
3. Uses `envFrom: openclaw-api-keys` to read the API key for rejection

Runs on every pod start, ensuring Claude Code is always correctly configured.

author: copilot
body:
When a project has `paper-write` or `paper-review` in its pipeline, `/neuroflow` had no mechanism to surface a missing target journal until the user actually ran `/paper-write`. This adds a proactive check at startup with an optional journal recommendation workflow.

## Changes

### `commands/neuroflow.md` — New Step 0b: Journal check
- Triggers when `paper-write` or `paper-review` is the active phase **or** appears in `recommended_phases`
- Looks for `target_journal:` in `project_config.md`, then falls back to `paper-write/flow.md`
- If set: prints it inline with the status summary
- If unset: prompts the user; on "Y" runs a full recommendation workflow:
  - Reads modality, research question, and keywords from `project_config.md` + `ideation/`
  - Searches PubMed + bioRxiv via `neuroflow:scholar` (past 3 years; recurring = ≥3/top-20 hits)
  - Ranks 3–5 journals by scope alignment → paper type → OA → length → prestige/speed
  - Writes chosen journal to `project_config.md`; also to `paper-write/flow.md` **only if the file already exists**

### `skills/phase-paper-write/SKILL.md` — New `## Journal recommendation` section
- Same search-and-rank workflow available when the skill is invoked directly via `/paper-write`
- Explicit recency (past 3 years) and recurrence (≥3 of top 20) thresholds added

### Version bump `0.1.7` → `0.1.8`
- Updated in `plugin.json`, `mkdocs.yml`, and `README.md`

body:
# Blockchain Supply Chain Transparency for Apparel Industry

## Summary

This pull request adds a comprehensive smart contract system that establishes end-to-end visibility for garment production. The solution creates an immutable audit trail from raw material sourcing through final consumer delivery, addressing the growing demand for ethical manufacturing verification.

## Motivation

The fashion industry faces increasing pressure to demonstrate ethical practices and transparent supply chains. Consumers want to verify sustainability claims, brands need to validate supplier compliance, and manufacturers require streamlined documentation processes. Traditional paper-based tracking systems are fragmented, easily falsified, and lack real-time visibility.

## Technical Overview

The smart contract architecture provides:

- **Material Origin Tracking**: Records raw material sources with certification validation, sustainability metrics, and supplier credentials
- **Manufacturing Verification**: Manages facility registration, production stage documentation, and compliance certification tracking
- **Supply Chain Checkpoints**: Captures transfer events, quality inspections, and handler verification at each stage
- **Consumer Query Interface**: Enables product history retrieval, authenticity verification, and certification access

## Key Components

### Data Structures

The contract defines comprehensive data maps for materials, manufacturers, products, and checkpoints. Each entity stores relevant metadata including certifications, locations, timestamps, and verification status.

### Authorization System

A permission-based model ensures only verified participants can add records. The contract owner manages participant authorization, while individual entities control their own data updates.

### Tracking Functions

Public functions allow authorized participants to register materials, create products, add manufacturing stages, and record supply chain checkpoints. All operations validate authorization and data integrity.

### Query Functions

Read-only functions provide transparent access to complete product histories, material origins, manufacturer details, and checkpoint records without compromising data security.

## Security Considerations

- Authorization required for all write operations
- Immutable records prevent tampering
- Manufacturer verification before product creation
- Quality checks at each checkpoint
- Product completion requires current handler authorization

## Testing

The contract passes syntax validation with clarinet check. Comprehensive unit tests verify:
- Authorization flows
- Material registration with various certification combinations
- Manufacturer registration and status updates
- Product creation and lifecycle management
- Checkpoint recording and history tracking
- Query functions for all entity types

## Documentation

Complete README provides usage examples, technical specifications, and integration guidance for supply chain participants.

## Benefits

**For Brands**: Verify supplier claims, demonstrate ethical practices, build consumer trust

**For Consumers**: Access complete product history, verify sustainability claims, make informed decisions

**For Suppliers**: Demonstrate compliance, build reputation, streamline documentation

## Future Considerations

- IoT sensor integration for automated checkpoint recording
- Mobile application for consumer QR code scanning
- Analytics dashboard for supply chain optimization
- Carbon footprint calculation and tracking
- Circular economy and waste tracking extensions

## Line Count

352 lines of clean, well-documented Clarity code with comprehensive functionality

author: rpalcolea
body:
Fixes #35389 

### Context

Publishing artifacts (PUT) through authenticated HTTP proxies can fail with "Broken pipe" errors, especially for large uploads. This happens because the  proxy challenges with 407 (Proxy Authentication Required) while the client is already streaming the request body — the proxy closes the connection mid-upload.

This PR enables HTTP/1.1 `Expect: 100-Continue` when proxy credentials are configured. With this header, the client sends only the request headers first and waits for the proxy to respond. If the proxy needs authentication, it replies with 407 *before* the body is sent, avoiding the broken pipe. Once authenticated, the client receives `100 Continue` and streams the body safely.

author: copilot
body:
The `InMemoryQueueTransportPump` used a polling loop with a 10ms delay to consume messages, creating a timing-dependent race condition that caused intermittent test failures even after #1673.

## Changes

- **New `InMemoryMessageQueue`**: replaces raw `ConcurrentQueue<string>` with a wrapper pairing it with a `SemaphoreSlim`. `Enqueue` releases the semaphore; `DequeueAsync` awaits it — the pump wakes up *immediately* on message arrival instead of on the next poll interval.

- **`InMemoryQueueTransportPump`**: replaced the `TryDequeue` + `Task.Delay` busy-loop with a single `await _queue.DequeueAsync(ct)`. `OperationCanceledException` is now caught explicitly so pump shutdown is clean.

- **`InMemoryQueueTransportBindingElement` / `InMemoryQueueIntegrationTests`**: updated DI registration and resolution to use `InMemoryMessageQueue`.

```csharp
// Before: polling with arbitrary delay
while (!ct.IsCancellationRequested)
{
    if (_queue.TryDequeue(out string message))
        await OnConsume(message, queueTransportContext);
    else
        await Task.Delay(EmptyQueueDelayMs, ct); // race window
}

// After: event-driven, zero latency
string message = await _queue.DequeueAsync(ct); // blocks until item available
await OnConsume(message, queueTransportContext);
```

author: copilot
body:
Multiple `std::stoul` call sites across the codebase were unprotected, risking `std::invalid_argument` or `std::out_of_range` exceptions from malformed user input (color strings, CLI args, config values). Existing catch blocks in several places silently swallowed failures with no diagnostic output.

## Changes

- **New try/catch blocks** — wrapped all unprotected `std::stoul` calls; on failure, log via `ywarn` and return a safe default (e.g. `0xFFFFFFFF` for colors, `0` for counts):
  - Color parsing: `yaml2ydraw.cpp`, `yaml2ypaint.cpp`, `ygrid.cpp`, `ygui.cpp`, `qrcode.cpp`, `ytext.cpp`
  - CLI arg parsing: `ypdf.cpp`, `ypaint.cpp`, `ydraw.cpp`, `yhtml.cpp`, `markdown.cpp`, `plot.cpp`, `diagram.cpp`
  - Misc: `msdf-wgsl/compare/main.cpp` (uses `fprintf` — no ytrace available)

- **ywarn added to silent catch blocks** — existing catches that discarded failures now emit a warning:
  - `zoo-renderer.cpp`, `maze-renderer.cpp`, `shader-manager.cpp`, `shader-font.cpp`, `yecho-parser.cpp`, `gpu-monitor.cpp`, `plot.cpp` (buffer size), `ygui-overlay.cpp`

- **ytrace include added** where `ywarn` was introduced but the header was missing: `yaml2ydraw.cpp`, `zoo-renderer.cpp`, `maze-renderer.cpp`, `yecho-parser.cpp`

**Before / after example (`ydraw.cpp`):**
```cpp
// Before — throws on bad input
_buffer->setBgColor(static_cast<uint32_t>(std::stoul(colorStr, nullptr, 16)));

// After — logs and continues
try {
    _buffer->setBgColor(static_cast<uint32_t>(std::stoul(colorStr, nullptr, 16)));
} catch (...) {
    ywarn("YDraw: failed to parse --bg-color value '{}'", colorStr);
}
```

# InternDAO - Decentralized Internship Network Implementation

## 🎯 Overview
This PR implements InternDAO, a comprehensive decentralized internship network that connects students with verified industry placements through blockchain technology. The platform ensures transparency, trust, and verified credentials for all internship opportunities.

## 🚀 Features Implemented

### Core Smart Contract Functionality
- **Company Registration System**: Complete company profile management with industry verification
- **Student Profile Management**: Comprehensive student registration with academic credentials
- **Internship Marketplace**: Full-featured internship posting and management system
- **Application Processing**: End-to-end application submission and review workflow
- **Certificate Issuance**: Blockchain-verified completion certificates with performance ratings
- **Rating & Review System**: Mutual rating system for companies and students
- **Data Integrity**: Robust error handling and input validation throughout

### Technical Implementation
- **583+ lines of clean Clarity code** with comprehensive functionality
- **Multiple data structures**: Companies, Students, Internships, Applications, Certificates
- **Security-first approach**: Access controls, input validation, and error handling
- **Efficient data management**: Optimized mappings and counter systems
- **Read-only functions**: Comprehensive getter functions for all data structures

## 🏗️ Architecture

### Data Models
1. **Companies**: Profile, verification status, ratings, contact information
2. **Students**: Academic credentials, skills, experience, performance tracking  
3. **Internships**: Job details, requirements, application limits, deadlines
4. **Applications**: Student applications with status tracking and review process
5. **Certificates**: Verified completion records with performance metrics

### Core Workflows
1. **Registration**: Companies and students create verified profiles
2. **Posting**: Companies create internship opportunities with detailed requirements
3. **Application**: Students apply with cover letters, subject to limits and deadlines
4. **Review**: Companies review applications and accept/reject candidates
5. **Completion**: Successful internships result in blockchain certificates
6. **Rating**: Mutual feedback system builds reputation and trust

## ✅ Quality Assurance
- All contracts pass `clarinet check` validation
- Comprehensive error handling with descriptive error codes
- Input validation on all user-provided data
- Access controls prevent unauthorized operations
- Clean, readable code with proper documentation

## 📁 File Structure
```
intern-dao/
├── README.md                 # Comprehensive project documentation

```

- Contract successfully compiles with `clarinet check`

- Error handling tested through validation
- Ready for comprehensive unit testing

## 💡 Next Steps
1. Implement comprehensive test suite
2. Add frontend integration
3. Deploy to testnet for live testing
4. Add advanced features like multi-sig verification
5. Implement search and filtering capabilities

This implementation provides a solid foundation for a decentralized internship network with all core features needed for production use.

### Motivation
- Jobs submitted from another Linux user on the same host were being attributed to the service owner when the UI was opened via `127.0.0.1`, causing incorrect `user_id` for jobs.

### Description
- Changed `get_system_user` to try request header user, then resolve the loopback socket owner, then fall back to existing `os.getlogin`/env/`pwd.getpwuid(os.getuid())` logic by default.
- Added socket-based loopback resolution helpers: `_is_loopback_host`, `_ipv4_hex`, `_parse_proc_tcp_uid` and `_get_local_socket_user`, and imported `socket` in `app.py`.
- The new logic inspects `/proc/net/tcp` for the local connection entry, maps the connection UID to a Linux username, and returns that username when the client and server are loopback addresses; IPv6 or unresolved cases fall back to prior behavior.

author: copilot
body:
`sftp -b <file>` internally passes `-oBatchMode=yes` to SSH, which disables all interactive authentication (password/keyboard-interactive). Every `sshpass`-based workaround fails for this reason — not because of pipe/PTY mechanics, but because SSH itself refuses the password exchange before `sshpass` can provide it.

The server supports `publickey` auth (confirmed via `ssh -v`). SSH key auth is unaffected by `BatchMode=yes`, making it the only mechanism compatible with unattended `sftp -b`.

### Changes
- **Drop `sshpass`**: remove `apt-get install sshpass`, `SFTP_PASSWORD`/`SSHPASS` env var, and all `~/.ssh/config` auth-override stanzas
- **Add SSH key auth**: write `SFTP_PRIVATE_KEY` secret to `~/.ssh/id_ed25519` (`chmod 600`); `sftp -b` picks it up automatically
- **Temp file cleanup**: use `trap 'rm -f "$SFTP_BATCH"' EXIT` so the batch file is removed even on failure

> **Required**: add an `SFTP_PRIVATE_KEY` Actions secret containing the Ed25519 private key whose public key is authorized on the SFTP server.
